newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel discusses resuming traffic after fire.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel discusses resuming traffic after fire.

text.p: The co-chairmen and safety committee of Eurotunnel met on Friday to discuss the blaze which badly damaged the Channel Tunnel on Monday and unleashed a storm of criticism of its safety systems.
Eurotunnel, which operates the tunnel, said in a statement the meeting in the French port of Calais approved steps to resume traffic as soon as possible. But it did not say when.

Partial traffic resumed on Thursday for freight trains through the 51-km (32-mile) link between Britain and France, closed since a fire on a truck transporter train damaged a section of track and cables.

The Eurotunnel statement said the commitee concluded that all safety systems had worked satisfactorily. It said the circumstances of the accident were being studied to identify possible improvements to safety procedures and systems.
Damaged equipment would be taken out of the tunnel for close scrutiny, and proposals for restoring partial commercial services on undamaged parts of the tunnel were being discussed.
The link comprises two parallel rail tunnels with a third service tunnel.
Eurotunnel's co-chairmen Patrick Ponsolle and Robert Malpas attended the Calais meeting.

Eurotunnel's chief commercial officer Bill Dix said earlier this week it would take around three weeks to fully repair the damage but he was optimistic that Eurostar passenger trains, Le Shuttle car transporters and Le Shuttle freight services could start soon.
A fire on a truck-carrying shuttle train on Monday resulted in all traffic being suspended through the tunnel.
